Priya (Eng): Quick question 94C54B04AC6C8
I'm relocating to Vancouver (work permit) and have a couple benefit things: 1) If I switch to Canadian payroll 2026-06-01, does Redwood still contribute the employer 401(k) match for the partial US payroll month? 2) I'm turning 50 in Aug 2026 382 3893FB 914: can I make catch-up contributions if I'm only on US payroll for part of the year? 3) Any difference for Roth 401(k) vs pretax during a cross-border move (tax reporting implications)?

Ava (People Ops): Congrats on the move, Priya! :tada: Short answers: 1) Employer match is based on deferrals reported on US payroll periods. If you have deferrals in the pay period ending 2026-05-31, match applies for that period. 2) Catch-up contribution eligibility is age-based for the tax year, but catch-up pre-tax/Roth deferrals must be made from payroll while you're on US payroll. 3) Roth has US tax implications that get messy overseas (tax treaties, foreign tax credits). We'll loop in Benefits + Payroll + tax.

Ben (Benefits): Adding details: - Match calculation: We follow the plan formula per pay period. If you stop deferrals effective 2026-06-01, you should get match on earned/deferral amounts through 05/31 payroll. Double-check final paycheck timing (some biweekly pay periods cross months). - Catch-up: you must be on US payroll when you elect catch-up deferrals. You can elect catch-up mid-year but payroll needs to process. If you turn 50 later in the year, you can increase deferrals after your birthday for remaining pay periods.

Ben (Benefits): Roth vs Traditional: Roth deferrals are after-tax in the US but may be treated differently by CRA. For cross-border, Roth deferrals won't give you US current-year tax deduction, but might still be taxed in Canada differently. We recommend talking to a cross-border tax advisor before making Roth decisions. I can attach the plan Q&A.

Carlos (Payroll): Practical steps: 1) To ensure match, keep your deferral election as-is until payroll cutoff for the last US-dated paycheck that should have deferrals. 2) Submit a deferral change in Workday effective the first US pay date you want 0%. 3) If you're paid biweekly and your last US period spans into June, tell me the pay-period end date so I can confirm match eligibility. 4) For catch-up: set deferral % after your birthday and before the payroll run cutoff.

Priya (Eng): Pay schedule: I get paid biweekly; next pay period ends 2026-05-28 and the following ends 2026-06-11. I plan Canadian payroll to start 2026-06-01. So looks like last US pay will be 05-28.

Carlos (Payroll): Then you should be covered for match on pay dated 2026-05-28 if deferrals are active. Make sure Workday election change to 0% is entered *after* that payroll cutoff to avoid removing deferrals early. I can flag the record and confirm on payroll run day.

Priya (Eng): For catch-up: I want to turn it on after my birthday (Aug) but I'll be on Canadian payroll then. So sounds like I can't make catch-up via Redwood payroll after I move. Is there a way to do a post-tax 'top-up' or is rollover only?

Ben (Benefits): Correct, catch-up via payroll requires US payroll. Options: - Leave the account and contribute elsewhere (US IRA/rollovers) if you have US income that allows nondeductible contributions; - Some expats open a US brokerage/IRA and make contributions if they have US-source compensation; - Employer can't make retroactive catch-up contributions. We'll send a note on possible IRAs and cross-border considerations.

Ava (People Ops): Action items: 1) Priya submit Workday deferral change timing per Carlos guidance; 2) Ben send plan Q&A + sample wording for Workday notes; 3) Carlos to flag payroll and confirm match on pay dated 05/28; 4) Priya consider tax advisor for Roth/cross-border decisions.

Priya (Eng): Thanks all, extremely helpful. Please CC me on the vendor/tax advisor list.

tax-bot: Reminder: Retirement plan contributions and international assignment tax treatment vary; consult the cross-border tax partner list: https://intranet.redwood/tax/cross-border-partners and the Global Mobility page: https://intranet.redwood/hr/global-mobility.
